study: One macaque: finger position from motor-cortex recordings (the LINK archive, six sessions of Monkey N)
what: Two finger positions predicted from recordings at 96 contacts in the hand area of motor cortex; fitted on four days, checked on two later days. Both networks lowered the average error and failed the rule fixed before fitting.

why_some_numbers_have_no_macro: Whole numbers below 100, and round numbers that double as percentages or durations elsewhere in the papers, have no macro: the build would otherwise refuse the same digits wherever another section types them as an ordinary number. The papers print them as words or as plain digits; each is listed here with its source so that it can be checked.
limits: One animal. The two checking days chose each network's stopping point, so these are development results, not a fresh test.
Four later recordings (22 and 24 February 2020; 21 and 22 June 2023) are reserved and have not been opened.
The unit is the archive's own finger-position scale (0 fully extended, 1 fully flexed, by the archive's description), not degrees or newtons.
The fitting has not been re-derived by an independent numerical route: the checks made after fitting recomputed the reported scores from the saved predictions.
The intervals describe these two days and these fitted networks; they are not estimates for another animal or another day.
